result.title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
result.summary: Long-horizon, semi-verifiable agentic tasks often rely on rubric-based evaluation, but the evidence needed to assess these tasks can be spread across the environment state and the execution trace. A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success. When rubric verdicts serve as reinforcement-learning rewards, such errors can reinforce undesirable behavior. We introduce Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier that investigates both state and trace and relies on a claim only after independently validating it against its source. Bounded queries and joint investigation of related criteria reduce context use and redundant work, and each verdict carries an auditable receipt of its supporting evidence. Across 2,586 human-labeled criteria from 100 personal-assistant episodes, Sauron achieves the highest F1 of five verifiers on all eight backbones tested while costing less than Gandalf, the strongest baseline. With GPT-5.6 Sol, it reaches 0.96 F1 versus Gandalf's 0.92 at 23% lower cost, with a wider margin on process criteria. On a paired fault-injection suite covering 13 families, several of which simulate reward hacking, Sauron detects 97% of injected failures while flagging only 2% of clean controls, outperforming baselines even when they are given the full trace. On TRAIL, a benchmark for detecting and localizing real agent errors, Sauron leads both Gandalf and TRAIL's own judge on all three quality metrics.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Sauron，一个「先取证后采信」的 agentic verifier：联合检查环境状态与执行轨迹，独立验证 claim 后才采信，用有界查询与相关标准的联合核查降低上下文开销，并为每条判定附可审计证据；在 2,586 条人工标注标准、故障注入套件和 TRAIL 上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其证据优先、逐条回溯来源的核查流程与可审计证据链，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、答案是否真正依赖 latent 内容的核验以及 RL 奖励的可靠性提供可借鉴的方法线索。
